definition.name: Blogging Platform
definition.overview:
A **Blogging Platform** is software for publishing an author-owned web publication — the blog — whose content is a dated stream of individually addressable posts.

The defining core is deliberately small:

```text
Author-owned Publication (the blog: stable identity + its own address)
└── Post (authored, dated, self-contained article — the unit of publication)
    └── Dated stream (posts presented as an ongoing archive ordered by publication time, newest-first by default)
        └── Per-post addressability (each post has its own stable URL)
```

Everything else commonly associated with blogging — editors, categories and tags, comments, themes, feeds, email delivery, memberships, analytics — is standard capability layered on that core, not part of what makes the product a blogging platform. The definition holds for the oldest hosted services of the late 1990s as well as for current creator-economy platforms.

When the primary object stops being the author's dated post stream — becoming arbitrary pages and content structures, a social follow-feed, or an email-first delivery product — the product has drifted toward a different Application Type (Content Management System, Microblogging Platform, or newsletter publishing).
definition.overview_zh:
一个**博客平台**是用于发布作者拥有的网络出版物——即博客——的软件，其内容是由可单独寻址的帖子组成的按日期排列的流。

其定义性核心被刻意保持精简：

```text
作者拥有的出版物（博客：稳定的身份 + 其自身的地址）
└── 帖子（已撰写、已标注日期、自包含的文章——发布的单元）
     └── 按日期排列的流（帖子作为按发布时间排序的持续存档呈现，默认最新优先）
         └── 每帖可寻址性（每个帖子拥有其自身的稳定 URL）
```

通常与博客相关的一切其他元素——编辑器、分类和标签、评论、主题、订阅源、电子邮件投递、会员资格、分析——都是叠加在该核心之上的标准功能，而非使该产品成为博客平台的部分。该定义既适用于 1990 年代末最古老的托管服务，也适用于当前的创作者经济平台。

当主要对象不再是作者的按日期排列的帖子流——而变成任意页面和内容结构、社交关注流，或以电子邮件为主的投递产品——该产品便已偏离至另一种应用类型（内容管理系统、微博平台或新闻通讯发布）。
definition.dc:
Four properties. If any one is removed, the product is no longer recognizable as a blogging platform:

- **Author-owned publication** — the blog is a persistent, titled, addressable publication owned by an identified author or team. Without it, content dissolves into an anonymous feed or a platform-owned network surface.
- **Post as the unit of publication** — a self-contained authored article (long-form text with embedded media), published as a discrete dated entry. Without it, the product is a microblog (short status updates) or a page-based website.
- **Dated stream** — the publication's organizing principle is publication time: posts accumulate as an ongoing, browsable archive, newest-first by default (some products allow reordering, so the direction is the common default rather than a requirement). Without it, the product is a general website.
- **Per-post addressability** — every post has its own stable URL that can be linked, shared, and cited. Without it, there is no citable publication unit.
definition.dc_zh:
四个属性。如果移除任何一个，产品就不再被识别为博客平台：

- **作者拥有的出版物** — 博客是由一个已识别作者或团队拥有的持久、有标题、可寻址的出版物。如果没有它，内容会溶解成匿名的 feed 或平台拥有的网络界面。

- **帖子作为出版的单位** — 一个独立撰写的长文文章（长文本与嵌入媒体），作为离散的日期条目发布。如果没有它，产品是微型博客（短状态更新）或基于页面的网站。

- **带日期的流** — 出版物的组织原则是发布时间：帖子作为持续、可浏览的档案积累，默认按最新排序（一些产品允许重排序，所以方向是常见默认而不是要求）。如果没有它，产品是通用网站。

- **每个帖子的可寻址性** — 每个帖子都有自己的稳定 URL，可以链接、分享和引用。如果没有它，就没有可引用的出版单位。
definition.rules:
### Posts and pages are different objects

Posts belong to the dated stream and its archives; pages are standalone and appear only where the author links them (menus, homepage). This distinction is structural in the researched products, not cosmetic.

### Publishing triggers distribution

Publishing a post is not just a visibility flip: it places the post at the top of the stream, enters it into feeds, and — where configured — sends email to subscribers and shares it externally. Editing a published post afterwards does not re-trigger these notifications.

### Published posts remain editable

A post's URL stays stable while its content can be corrected or updated after publication. The blog is a living document, in contrast to print-era publication.

### Comments are optional and governed

Commenting is controlled per post and site-wide, with approval and spam machinery. A blog without comments is still fully a blog; a forum without an owning author is not.

### The stream is the archive

The publication's value accumulates: older posts remain reachable through archives, search, and permalinks rather than disappearing from view as new posts arrive.

### Visibility can be gated

Products commonly support private sites, password-protected posts, or member-only content — the publication model survives, with access control layered on top.
definition.rules_zh:
### 帖子和页面是不同的对象

帖子属于按日期排列的流及其存档；页面是独立的，仅出现在作者链接它们的地方（菜单、主页）。在研究过的产品中，这种区别是结构性的，而非表面上的。

### 发布触发分发

发布帖子不仅仅是可见性开关：它将帖子置于流的顶部，将其纳入订阅源，并且——在配置的情况下——向订阅者发送电子邮件并对外分享。之后编辑已发布的帖子不会重新触发这些通知。

### 已发布的帖子仍可编辑

帖子的 URL 在内容可在发布后更正或更新时保持稳定。博客是一份活着的文档，与印刷时代的出版物形成对比。

### 评论是可选且受控的

评论按帖子和全站范围进行控制，具有批准和垃圾信息机制。没有评论的博客仍然是完全的博客；没有拥有作者的论坛则不是。

### 流即存档

出版物的价值是累积的：较旧的帖子通过存档、搜索和永久链接保持可访问，而不是随着新帖子的到来而从视野中消失。

### 可见性可被门控

产品通常支持私有站点、密码保护的帖子或仅限成员的内容——出版物模式得以保留，并在其上叠加访问控制。

definition.name: Content Management System / CMS
definition.overview:
A **Content Management System (CMS)** is software through which an organization creates, structures, stores, and manages digital content items, and assembles them into a delivered website — without requiring the people who write the content to write code.

The defining core is small:

```text
Structured content items (typed, field-based)
  stored in a managed content repository
    authored by non-developers in an administrative interface
      assembled into delivered web pages by a coupled presentation layer
        moved through a controlled publishing lifecycle
```

Everything else commonly associated with CMS products — media libraries, categories and tags, revision history, menus, SEO tooling, multilingual content, plugin ecosystems, headless APIs, personalization — is widely supported by mature products but is not what makes a product a CMS. Older, regional, and platform-native CMS products satisfy the definition without most of those capabilities, and modern products add them without changing what the Type is.

When the coupled presentation layer is removed and content is delivered only through APIs, the product becomes a different Application Type (Headless CMS). When the structured content repository is removed and only visual page construction remains, it becomes a Website Builder.
definition.overview_zh:
一个**内容管理系统（CMS）**是一种软件，组织通过它创建、构建、存储和管理数字内容项，并将它们组装成交付的网站——而不需要撰写内容的人员编写代码。

其定义性核心很小：

```text
结构化的内容项（带类型、基于字段）
  存储在受管理的内容存储库中
    由非开发人员通过管理界面撰写
      由耦合的表示层组装成交付的网页
        通过受控的发布生命周期进行流转
```

通常与 CMS 产品相关联的其他所有内容——媒体库、分类和标签、修订历史、菜单、SEO 工具、多语言内容、插件生态系统、无头 API、个性化——虽然被成熟产品广泛支持，但这并不是使一个产品成为 CMS 的原因。较旧的、区域性的以及平台原生的 CMS 产品在没有这些大部分功能的情况下也满足定义，而现代产品增加了这些功能，但并未改变其类型。

当耦合的表示层被移除，内容仅通过 API 交付时，该产品就变成了另一种应用类型（无头 CMS）。当结构化的内容存储库被移除，仅保留可视化页面构建时，它就变成了网站构建器。
definition.dc:
Four structures. If any one is removed, the product is no longer recognizable as a CMS:

- **Structured content items** — content exists as discrete, typed items with fields (a news item with a headline, body, date, and image; a product page; a landing page), not as loose files or raw code. Typing is what lets the system list, relate, reuse, and re-present content.
- **Content repository** — the persistent store where items live, together with their media assets and organizational metadata. The repository is the system of record: the website is a projection of it.
- **Editor-facing authoring interface** — an administrative surface (the "back end") where non-developers create and edit items through forms, rich-text editors, or block editors. This is what distinguishes a CMS from a web framework.
- **Coupled presentation layer** — the same system renders stored content into the public website ("front end") through templates, themes, and components. The CMS owns both the content and its delivery: change the content, and the site updates; change the theme, and the content re-presents.
- **Publishing lifecycle** — items move through managed states: work-in-progress (draft) → published → updated → archived or unpublished. The published state is a visibility switch controlled by the system, not by the file system.
definition.dc_zh:
四个结构。如果移除任何一个，产品将不再被识别为CMS：
- **结构化内容项** — 内容以离散、有类型的项存在，带有字段（如新闻项目包含标题、正文、日期和图像；产品页面；着陆页），而不是松散文件或原始代码。类型化使系统能够列出、关联、重用和重新呈现内容。
- **内容存储库** — 持久存储，项驻留其中，连同其媒体资产和组织元数据。存储库是记录系统：网站是其投影。
- **面向编辑器的创作界面** — 管理表面（“后端”），非开发者通过表单、富文本编辑器或块编辑器创建和编辑项。这区分了CMS和Web框架。
- **耦合的呈现层** — 同一系统通过模板、主题和组件将存储的内容渲染到公共网站（“前端”）。CMS拥有内容和其传递：更改内容，网站更新；更改主题，内容重新呈现。
- **发布生命周期** — 项通过受管理的状态移动：进行中（草稿）→ 已发布 → 已更新 → 已归档或未发布。已发布状态是由系统控制的可见性开关，而不是文件系统。
definition.rules:
### Draft and published are different worlds

An unpublished draft is invisible to the public site no matter how complete it is. Preview exists precisely because the editor must see the published rendering without publishing. Conversely, unpublishing removes public visibility but keeps the item in the repository — removal from the site is not deletion of the record.

### Content and presentation are separable

The same content renders under whatever theme or template is active. Changing the presentation layer re-presents the repository without rewriting it; changing content does not require touching templates. This separation is the CMS's central engineering idea and the reason editors and developers can work independently.

### Publishing is permission-gated

In mature products, the right to edit and the right to publish are distinct permissions. An editor may be able to save drafts that only a publisher can release. Access rights also gate scheduling and section-level administration.

### Revisions are the safety net

Every significant save produces a version. Editors can compare and revert. Published-but-wrong content is corrected by publishing a new version, not by editing history.

### URLs are managed, not incidental

Content items have system-managed addresses (permalinks). Products provide redirect management because moving or renaming content must not break inbound links — the URL structure is part of the managed content model.

### The repository is the system of record

Lists, archives, topic pages, and feeds are generated views over the repository (for example, a category page listing its items). Deleting or unpublishing an item changes every view that includes it.
definition.rules_zh:
### 草稿和发布是不同的世界

无论多么完整，未发布的草稿对公共站点都是不可见的。预览的存在正是为了让编辑能够在不发布的情况下看到发布后的渲染效果。相反，取消发布会移除公共可见性，但将条目保留在存储库中——从站点移除并非删除记录。

### 内容和表示是可分离的

相同的内容在活动的任何主题或模板下渲染。更改表示层会重新呈现存储库而无需重写它；更改内容不需要触及模板。这种分离是 CMS 的核心工程理念，也是编辑和开发人员可以独立工作的原因。

### 发布受权限门控

在成熟产品中，编辑权限和发布权限是独立的权限。编辑可能能够保存草稿，但只有发布者才能发布。访问权限还门控计划安排和章节级管理。

### 修订是安全网

每次重大保存都会产生一个版本。编辑可以比较和还原。已发布但错误的内容通过发布新版本来纠正，而不是通过编辑历史。

### URL 是受管理的，而非偶然的

内容项具有系统管理的地址（永久链接）。产品提供重定向管理，因为移动或重命名内容不能破坏传入链接——URL 结构是受管理内容模型的一部分。

### 存储库是记录系统

列表、归档、主题页面和源是存储库上的生成视图（例如，列出其条目的分类页面）。删除或取消发布条目会更改包含它的每个视图。

definition.name: Headless CMS
definition.overview:
A **Headless CMS** is a content management system that stores and manages structured content in a repository that is deliberately decoupled from presentation. Content is created against a customer-defined content model, and delivered to websites, apps, and other digital channels through APIs — while the end-user-facing interface (the "head") is built outside the product by the consuming team.

It solves a specific problem: organizations whose content must flow into multiple, independently built digital properties (websites, mobile apps, kiosks, in-store screens) need a single place where content is structured, authored, reviewed, and published — without that place also owning how pages look. A traditional CMS couples the content repository with page rendering; a headless CMS removes the rendering half and exposes the repository through APIs instead.

The defining structure is small:

```text
Content model (content types with typed fields — defined by the customer)
└── Content entries stored against the model
    ├── References between entries
    └── Media assets
        ↓ delivered as
Read APIs (published content)  ← consumed by  →  External frontends (built outside)
Management APIs (create/update/publish)
```

Everything else commonly associated with the category — CDN delivery, GraphQL, visual editing, AI assistance, app marketplaces — is widespread in current products but is not what makes the product a headless CMS.
definition.overview_zh:
一个 **Headless CMS** 是一种内容管理系统，它将结构化内容存储并管理在一个刻意与展示层解耦的存储库中。内容基于客户定义的内容模型进行创建，并通过 API 交付到网站、应用程序及其他数字渠道——而面向最终用户的界面（即“头部”）则由消费方团队在产品外部构建。

它解决了一个特定问题：那些内容必须流入多个独立构建的数字资产（网站、移动应用、自助终端、店内屏幕）的组织，需要一个单一的地方来结构化、编写、审核和发布内容——而这个地方不负责页面的外观。传统 CMS 将内容存储库与页面渲染耦合在一起；Headless CMS 则去除了渲染部分，转而通过 API 暴露存储库。

其定义性结构很小：

```text
内容模型（具有类型化字段的内容类型——由客户定义）
└── 基于模型存储的内容条目
     ├── 条目之间的引用
     └── 媒体资产
         ↓ 交付为
读取 API（已发布内容）   ← 被消费于   →  外部前端（在外部构建）
管理 API（创建/更新/发布）
```

通常与该类别相关联的其他一切——CDN 交付、GraphQL、可视化编辑、AI 辅助、应用市场——在当前产品中很普遍，但这并不是使该产品成为 Headless CMS 的原因。
definition.dc:
Four structures. If any one is removed, the product is no longer recognizable as a headless CMS:

- **Content model** — a schema of *content types* (for example: article, product page, author, navigation menu), each made of *typed fields* (text, rich text, numbers, dates, locations, media, references to other entries) with validation rules. The model is defined by the implementing team, not fixed by the product, and is defined independently of any page design. Without it, the product is a generic database.
- **Content entries** — the items of content created and stored against the model. Entries link to each other through *reference fields* (an article references its author; a page references its components) and to *media assets* (images, video, documents) held in an attached asset store. Entries — not pages — are the system of record.
- **API delivery** — published content is retrieved programmatically through a read API by the external frontends; content is created and managed through a management API (which the product's own editorial application typically uses as well). The API is the primary delivery surface.
- **Decoupled presentation** — the product does not render the end-user experience. Frontends are built outside it. Preview and visual-editing features render the *external* frontend showing draft content; they assist editing but are not the delivery surface.
definition.dc_zh:
四大结构。移除任何一项，该产品将不再被识别为无头CMS：
- **内容模型** — 一种定义内容类型模式的架构（例如：文章、产品页面、作者、导航菜单），每种类型由具有验证规则的类型化字段（文本、富文本、数字、日期、位置、媒体、其他条目的引用）组成。该模型由实施团队定义，而非由产品固定，且独立于任何页面设计。若无此模型，该产品即为通用数据库。
- **内容条目** — 基于模型创建和存储的内容项目。条目通过引用字段相互关联（一篇文章引用其作者；一个页面引用其组成部分），并与存储在附加资产库中的媒体资产（图像、视频、文档）关联。条目（而非页面）才是系统的记录本源。
- **API交付** — 已发布的内容通过读取API供外部前端以编程方式获取；内容通过管理API创建和管理（产品自身的编辑应用程序通常也使用此API）。API是主要的交付界面。
- **表现层解耦** — 该产品不渲染最终用户体验。前端在其外部构建。预览和可视化编辑功能渲染显示草稿内容的外部前端；它们辅助编辑但并非交付界面。
definition.rules:
- **Publish is the delivery gate.** The public read API serves published content only. Drafts are never exposed through it; they are visible only inside the editorial application (and through authenticated preview mechanisms).
- **Draft and published versions coexist.** Editing a published entry creates draft changes while the published version keeps serving; publishing applies the draft. Unpublishing withdraws the public version, with products differing on whether the last draft is kept or replaced.
- **Model changes reach into existing content.** Adding a field makes it available on existing entries (typically empty until filled); required-field validation usually applies at the next edit/publish of an old entry rather than retroactively breaking it. Deleting a model element is guarded — products commonly require a disable/deactivate step first, because consuming frontends depend on the shape of the API response.
- **References must be published to resolve.** An entry referencing an unpublished entry may deliver without the referenced content; publishing related content together (or via releases) is a routine operational concern.
- **Edit and publish are separately permissioned.** The classic role split — writers draft, editors/publishers release — is supported through roles in mature products; API credentials are scoped separately from user accounts.
- **Webhooks report content changes.** External systems learn about publishes, unpublishes, and other changes through webhook events; delivery caching is the frontend's responsibility to invalidate.
- **Containers isolate change.** Model and content changes made in a staging container do not affect production until promoted; the container mechanism (environments, datasets, instances) varies but the isolation behavior is standard.
definition.rules_zh:
- **发布是交付关口。** 公共读取 API 仅提供已发布内容。草稿永远不会通过它暴露；它们仅在编辑应用程序内部（以及通过经过身份验证的预览机制）可见。
- **草稿和已发布版本共存。** 编辑已发布条目会创建草稿更改，而已发布版本继续提供服务；发布应用草稿。取消发布会撤回公共版本，产品在是否保留或替换最后一个草稿方面存在差异。
- **模型更改影响现有内容。** 添加字段使其在现有条目上可用（通常为空直到填写）；必填字段验证通常在旧条目的下一次编辑/发布时应用，而不是追溯性地破坏它。删除模型元素受到保护——产品通常要求先执行禁用/停用步骤，因为消费前端依赖于 API 响应的结构。
- **引用必须发布才能解析。** 引用未发布条目的条目可能在交付时不包含被引用内容；一起发布相关内容（或通过发布）是常规的运营关注点。
- **编辑和发布具有单独的权限。** 经典的角色划分——编写者起草，编辑/发布者发布——在成熟产品中通过角色得到支持；API 凭据与用户账户分开限定范围。
- **Webhooks 报告内容更改。** 外部系统通过 webhook 事件了解发布、取消发布和其他更改；交付缓存的失效是前端的职责。
- **容器隔离更改。** 在预发布容器中进行的模型和内容更改在提升之前不会影响生产环境；容器机制（环境、数据集、实例）各不相同，但隔离行为是

definition.name: Product Documentation Portal
definition.overview:
A **Product Documentation Portal** is a managed publishing system through which a product's own team authors, organizes, publishes, and keeps current the documentation that teaches the product's audience how to use it.

It solves a specific publishing problem: a product changes with every release, its users need self-serve answers organized around the product rather than around a support queue, and the documentation must remain aligned with the thing it documents. The portal is therefore both a **writing environment** for the producer side and a **published reading site** for the product's users, administrators, and evaluators — one managed corpus with two deliberately separate surfaces.

The defining core is small:

```text
Product-usage documentation corpus
└── pages authored and maintained by the product's own team
    └── published as a self-serve reader surface (topical navigation tree + search)
        └── kept aligned with the product as it changes
            (managed production side + an explicit update/currency mechanism)
```

Remove the product-usage corpus and the system is a generic content repository or wiki. Remove the published reader surface and it is an internal authoring tool. Remove the machinery that keeps content current as the product ships and it is a hand-published page collection — and the corpus drifts out of step with the product, the canonical failure mode of this Type.
definition.overview_zh:
一个**产品文档门户**是一个受管理的发布系统，产品团队通过该系统撰写、组织、发布并持续维护文档，以教导产品的受众如何使用该产品。

它解决了一个特定的发布问题：产品随每次发布而变更，其用户需要围绕产品而非支持队列组织的自助式答案，且文档必须与其所记录的对象保持一致。因此，门户既是生产侧的**写作环境**，也是面向产品用户、管理员和评估者的**已发布阅读站点**——一个受管理的语料库，拥有两个刻意分离的界面。

其定义性核心很小：

```text
产品使用文档语料库
└── 由产品自身团队撰写和维护的页面
     └── 发布为自助阅读界面（主题导航树 + 搜索）
         └── 随产品变更而保持对齐
             （受管理的生产侧 + 明确的更新/时效机制）
```

移除产品使用语料库，该系统便成为通用的内容存储库或维基。移除已发布的阅读界面，它便成为内部写作工具。移除随产品发布而保持内容时效的机制，它便成为手工发布的页面集合——语料库将与产品脱节，这是该类型典型的失效模式。
definition.dc:
Three structures, held jointly:

**1. The product-usage documentation corpus of record.** A persistent, individually addressable set of pages — each page a maintained document with an identity, a location in the structure, and an editorial state. The corpus documents one specific product (or product line): what it does, how to get started, how each feature works, how to administer it, and what changed between releases. Authorship belongs to the producer side; readers react and suggest but never edit the record.

**2. The published navigable reader surface.** The corpus is published for self-serve reading — today realized as a branded website, usually on the product's own domain — organized the way readers consume it: a deliberate topical navigation tree (getting started → guides → reference → release notes), plus search over the whole corpus. Readers reach it directly — no staff mediation, no ticket required.

**3. The production-and-currency machinery.** A managed production side connects writing to publication: an integrated authoring-and-publishing platform, or a documentation-as-code pipeline over content repositories. On top of it sits an explicit mechanism that keeps the published corpus aligned with the product as it changes — release-coupled documentation versioning, changelog/release-notes integration, repository-coupled synchronization, or editorial workflows with scheduled reviews. The specific mechanism varies by product; that some explicit mechanism exists does not.
definition.dc_zh: 三个结构，共同持有：1. 产品使用文档记录库：一个持久、可单独寻址的页面集——每个页面都是维护的文档，具有标识、结构中的位置和编辑状态。该库文档记录一个特定产品（或产品线）：它的功能、如何入门、每个功能如何工作、如何管理它，以及版本之间的变更。作者属于生产方；读者反应和建议但从不编辑记录。2. 发布的可导航读者界面：该库发布供自助阅读——今天实现为品牌网站，通常在产品自己的域名上——按照读者消费的方式组织：一个有意的专题导航树（入门→指南→参考→发行说明），加上整个库的搜索。读者直接访问——无需工作人员中介，无需票证。3. 生产和时效机制：一个管理的生产端将写作与发布连接起来：一个集成的创作和发布平台，或者一个基于内容仓库的文档即代码流水线。其上存在一个明确的机制，保持发布的库与产品变化同步——发布耦合的文档版本控制、变更日志/发行说明集成、仓库耦合的同步，或带有调度的编辑工作流。
definition.rules:
### Published and draft states coexist per page

A live page always remains live while a new version is drafted, reviewed, or scheduled. The reader never sees an editing in-progress state; the contributor side always sees which pages have pending changes.

### Authorship is producer-side

Only the product's team edits the corpus. Readers influence it through feedback, ratings, suggestions, and support conversations — never by direct edits. (This is a structural difference from wikis and community forums.)

### The tree is structure, navigation, and access scope at once

The same hierarchy that orders reading also drives the site's URL scheme, its sitemap, and commonly its visibility rules: hiding a branch hides it from readers; access restrictions attach to sections and pages. Renaming or moving items is a structural operation with URL consequences, which is why mature products commonly carry redirect and link-integrity machinery.

### Currency is enforced, not assumed

The system carries explicit signals for out-of-date content — scheduled review reminders that mark pages stale, version badges for deprecated releases, update indicators shown to readers. The failure mode the machinery guards against is drift between the published corpus and the shipped product.

### Versioning is optional and deliberate

Whole-corpus versioning (a switcher with maintained documentation per product release) is common where readers run many product versions — and deliberately avoided where docs rarely change between releases. Its absence does not make a portal less of one; the underlying requirement is only that some mechanism keeps the corpus current.

### Machine-readability is part of the modern reader surface

Alongside the human site, current products expose the corpus in machine-oriented forms (Markdown page versions, generated index files, structured retrieval endpoints) so that search engines and AI agents can consume the same documentation. Readers increasingly arrive through those channels rather than through the site itself.
definition.rules_zh:
### 已发布与草稿状态每页共存

在线页面始终在草稿、审核或计划的新版本期间保持在线。读者永远不会看到编辑进行中的状态；贡献者侧始终能看到哪些页面有待处理的变更。

### 撰写权属于生产侧

只有产品团队编辑语料库。读者通过反馈、评分、建议和支持对话产生影响——绝不通过直接编辑。（这是与维基和社区论坛的结构差异。）

### 导航树同时是结构、导航和访问范围

同一层级结构既决定阅读顺序，也驱动站点的 URL 方案、站点地图，通常还驱动其可见性规则：隐藏分支即对读者隐藏；访问限制附加到章节和页面。重命名或移动项目是具有 URL 后果的结构操作，这就是成熟产品通常携带重定向和链接完整性机制的原因。

### 时效性由强制执行，而非假设

系统携带针对过时内容的明确信号——标记页面过时的计划审核提醒、针对弃用版本的版本徽章、向读者显示的更新指示器。该机制所防范的失效模式是已发布语料库与已发布产品之间的漂移。

### 版本控制是可选且刻意的

全语料库版本控制（具有每个产品发布维护文档的切换器）在读者运行多个产品版本时很常见——而在发布间文档很少变更时则刻意避免。其缺失并不使门户失去门户性质；底层要求仅是某种机制保持语料库时效。

### 机器可读性是现代读者界面的一部分

除了人类站点外，当前产品还以机器可

definition.name: Content Curation Platform
definition.overview:
A **Content Curation Platform** is a platform on which a curator captures discrete content items — most often references to articles, videos, images, social posts, or documents that live elsewhere on the web — selectively organizes them into persistent, named collections enriched with the curator's own context, and presents those collections to an audience through shareable or publishable surfaces.

The defining structure is small:

```text
Captured content items
  └── Curator's selective organization into persistent collections
        └── Audience-facing presentation of the collection
```

Everything commonly associated with modern curation products — suggestion engines that monitor sources, RSS feeds, auto-categorization, analytics, organizational governance, education templates, AI assistance — is widespread in current products but is not what makes the product a curation platform. Remove the curated collection as the managed artifact and the product becomes a feed reader or an aggregator; remove human selection and it becomes an aggregator; remove the audience-facing presentation and it becomes a personal bookmark manager.
definition.overview_zh:
一个**内容策展平台**是一个平台，策展人在此捕获离散的单项内容——通常是位于网络其他地方的文章、视频、图像、社交帖子或文档的引用——有选择地将它们组织成持久的、命名的集合，并辅以策展人自己的上下文，并通过可共享或可发布的界面将这些集合呈现给受众。

其定义性结构很小：

```text
捕获的内容项
   └── 策展人将其有选择地组织成持久集合
         └── 面向受众的集合展示
```

通常与现代策展产品相关的一切——监控来源的建议引擎、RSS 订阅、自动分类、分析、组织治理、教育模板、AI 辅助——在当前产品中很普遍，但这并不是使产品成为策展平台的原因。如果移除作为受管工件的策展集合，产品就变成了一个阅读器或聚合器；如果移除人工选择，它就变成了一个聚合器；如果移除面向受众的展示，它就变成了一个个人书签管理器。
definition.dc:
- **Collection** — the central managed artifact: a persistent, named, deliberately arranged set of items. Collections support ordering, grouping into sections, visual design (layouts, cover images), a descriptive introduction that tells the audience what the collection is for, and in many products nesting (collections inside collections). The collection — not a stream, not a folder of private links — is what the curator builds and maintains over time.
- **Curator** — the person (or team) exercising selection. The curator has a profile that acts as the public identity for their published collections. When curation is shared, the curator role expands into a small collaboration model with contributors and, in organizational settings, administrators.
- **Audience-facing presentation** — the collection rendered as a surface for people other than the curator: a public page, a share link, an embeddable widget, a generated newsletter, a team board. This is what separates curation from private bookmarking; the presentation surface is a first-class part of the product, not an afterthought.
definition.dc_zh:
集合 — 核心管理制品：一个持久的、命名的、精心安排的物品集合。集合支持排序、分组到部分、视觉设计（布局、封面图像）、一个描述性介绍，告诉受众集合的用途，并且在许多产品中支持嵌套（集合内的集合）。集合——不是一个流，不是一个私有链接的文件夹——是策展人随时间构建和维护的东西。
策展人 — 行使选择的人（或团队）。策展人有一个个人资料，作为他们发布集合的公共身份。当策展共享时，策展人角色扩展为一个小型协作模型，包括贡献者，在组织环境中包括管理员。
面向受众的呈现 — 集合渲染为对除策展人之外的其他人的表面：一个公共页面、一个分享链接、一个可嵌入的小部件、一个生成的通讯、一个团队板。这是将策展与私有书签区分开来的原因；呈现表面是产品的一等部分，不是事后添加。
definition.rules:
### Selection is human; automation assists

The defining behavior of the Type: what enters a collection is a curator's choice. Suggestion engines, auto-categorization, and content automation are common assists, but the collection remains a curated set. Products built purely on automated assembly — algorithmic "newspapers" with minimal per-item control — sat on the aggregator side of the boundary, and that pole has largely disappeared from today's market.

### The collection is the durable deliverable

Items and collections persist independently of any single session. The collection accumulates value over time — it is an archive as well as a presentation. Published surfaces can be live-linked to the collection, so maintaining the collection maintains the publication.

### Privacy is a per-collection decision

A curator typically runs a mix: private working collections, shared team collections, and public published ones. The default posture varies by product — community-oriented products tend to start collections public (visibility is part of their social design), while organizational products default to private. Moving a collection between these states is a supported, deliberate act.

### Items reference their sources

Because the raw material is other people's content, the platform's relationship with sources matters: items normally link back to the original content, curator additions are presented as context rather than replacement, some products support explicit author attribution when sharing, and some offer publishers a mechanism to opt out of being collected.

### Capture and organization are separate steps

Where a staging state exists, capture and organization are deliberately separated: items land unplaced and get organized later. The design lets curators collect quickly in the moment and curate deliberately afterwards.

### Collaboration has governance

Shared curation is governed by roles — who may add, edit, manage, or administer — and, in several products, by history that allows recovering items removed in error. In organizational deployments, workspace administrators control feature access and sharing permissions.
definition.rules_zh:
### 选择是人工的；自动化是辅助的

该类型的定义性行为：进入集合的是策展人的选择。建议引擎、自动分类和内容自动化是常见的辅助，但集合仍然是经过策展的集合。完全基于自动组装构建的产品——算法生成的“报纸”，对每个项目的控制极少——位于边界的聚合器一侧，而这一极在今天的市场中已基本消失。

### 集合是持久的交付物

项目和集合独立于任何单次会话而持久存在。集合随时间积累价值——它既是档案也是展示。发布界面可以与集合实时链接，因此维护集合即维护出版物。

### 隐私是逐集合的决定

策展人通常运行混合模式：私有工作集合、共享团队集合和公共发布集合。默认姿态因产品而异——面向社区的产品倾向于将集合设为公共（可见性是其社交设计的一部分），而组织型产品默认设为私有。在状态之间移动集合是一个受支持的、刻意的行为。

### 项目引用其来源

因为原材料是他人的内容，平台与来源的关系很重要：项目通常链接回原始内容，策展人的添加作为上下文而非替代呈现，一些产品在共享时支持明确的作者归属，一些为出版商提供退出被收集的机制。

### 捕获和组织是分开的步骤

在存在暂存状态的地方，捕获和组织被刻意分离：项目落地时未放置，稍后组织。这种设计让策展人能够收集

definition.name: Feed Reader
definition.overview:
A **Feed Reader** is a personal application for following published content. The user assembles their own list of sources — blogs, news sites, journals, podcasts, video channels, newsletters — and the reader continuously brings in whatever those sources publish, presenting the arriving items in a single reading surface with per-item reading state.

The defining core is small:

```text
User-managed subscription list
  └── Source (an external publisher the user chose)
        └── Item (what the source publishes: article, post, episode, video)
              └── Reading state (unread / read / saved)
```

Three properties make the Type what it is. **The user's own list** decides what enters the application — the reader's job is faithful intake of the sources the user chose, not selection on the user's behalf. **Standing automated intake** — new items arrive on their own as sources publish; nothing depends on the user remembering to check, and nothing needs to be captured by hand. **A consumption surface with reading state** — the reader shows what has arrived, tracks what has been read, and lets the user read in place or continue at the source.

The reader solves a specific problem: keeping up with many publishing sources without visiting each site in turn, without relying on memory, and — in the philosophy most products state explicitly — without an algorithm deciding what is worth seeing.

When the product's own machinery rather than the user's list decides what enters the surface, it is a Content Aggregator or a Personalized Content Feed. When items only appear through deliberate one-off saving, it is a Bookmark Manager. Those seams are described under Related Application Types.
definition.overview_zh:
一个**Feed Reader（订阅源阅读器）**是一个用于关注已发布内容的个人应用程序。用户自行汇编一份来源列表——包括博客、新闻网站、期刊、播客、视频频道、新闻通讯——阅读器会持续获取这些来源发布的内容，并将新到达的项目呈现在单一的阅读界面上，同时为每个项目维护阅读状态。

其定义性的核心结构很小：

```text
用户管理的订阅列表
   └── 来源（用户选择的外部发布者）
         └── 项目（来源发布的内容：文章、帖子、剧集、视频）
               └── 阅读状态（未读 / 已读 / 已保存）
```

三个特性决定了该类型的本质。**用户自己的列表**决定了哪些内容进入应用程序——阅读器的职责是忠实接收用户选择的来源，而非代替用户进行选择。**持续的自动化接收**——新项目随着来源的发布自动到达；不依赖用户记得去检查，也不需要手动捕获。**带有阅读状态的消费界面**——阅读器展示已到达的内容，追踪已读内容，并允许用户就地阅读或前往来源处继续阅读。

阅读器解决了一个具体问题：在不依次访问每个网站、不依赖记忆、并且——在大多数产品明确阐述的理念中——不依赖算法决定什么值得看的情况下，跟上众多发布来源的步伐。

当决定进入界面的内容是由产品自身的机制而非用户的列表决定时，它就是一个内容聚合器（Content Aggregator）或个性化内容信息流。当项目仅通过刻意的一次性保存出现时，它就是一个书签管理器。这些边界在“相关应用类型”部分有描述。
definition.dc:
**Subscription list.** The central managed object: a durable, personal list of content sources. The user adds sources, organizes them (folders, categories, or tags in most mature products), and prunes them. The list persists across sessions and — in networked products — across devices. It is simultaneously the user interface and the selector: nothing appears on the reading surface that does not trace back to an entry on this list.

**Source.** An external publisher whose stream the user follows. Conceptually it is any entity that publishes a sequence of items. The common implementation is a machine-readable feed in RSS, Atom, or JSON Feed format, but the concept is wider: some products also accept sources implemented as scraped web pages that have no feed, email addresses (newsletters delivered to a per-user intake address), YouTube channels and playlists, or social accounts.

**Item.** The unit a source publishes — an article, blog post, news story, episode, or video. An item typically carries a title, a publication date, the content itself or a synopsis, and a link back to the source. Feed formats identify each item so the reader can recognize an item it has already seen and not show it twice. Items may carry attached media (enclosures), which is how audio and video publishing travels through the same machinery. The item is owned by the source, not the reader: the reader's copy is a reference plus (usually) a stored rendering, and items often remain readable in the reader even after the source page changes.

**Reading state.** The per-item state machine that makes triage possible: unread until consumed, then read (with "keep unread" as the escape hatch), and a separate long-term layer for items worth keeping (starred / bookmarked). Aggregate unread counts per source and overall are the reader's pulse. This state belongs to the reader and the user — the source site knows nothing of it.
definition.dc_zh:
**订阅列表。** 核心管理对象：一个持久化的个人内容来源列表。用户可以添加、组织（在大多数成熟产品中为文件夹、分类或标签）和整理精简该列表。列表在会话间持久化存储，并可在联网产品中跨设备同步。它既是用户界面也是选择器：任何出现在阅读界面的内容都必须追溯到该列表中的条目。

**信息源。** 用户所关注的外部发布者。概念上，它可以是发布一系列条目的任何实体。常见实现是机器可读的 RSS、Atom 或 JSON Feed 格式，但概念更广泛：部分产品也支持无 feed 的抓取网页、电子邮件地址（通过每用户专用接收地址接收的新闻通讯）、YouTube 频道与播放列表，或社交账户等来源。

**条目。** 信息源发布的基本单元——可以是文章、博客文章、新闻故事、单集节目或视频。条目通常包含标题、发布日期、正文或摘要，以及返回信息源的链接。Feed 格式为每个条目标识，以便阅读器识别已显示的条目避免重复呈现。条目可附带媒体附件，这也是音频与视频通过同一机制传播的方式。条目由信息源而非读者所有：读者的协
definition.rules:
- **The list is the selector.** The reader shows what the user's subscriptions deliver — no editorial selection, no algorithmic insertion of unrequested items. Products differ in optional extras around this core, but the stream itself is the user's list made flesh. This is the structural line between a reader and an aggregator.
- **Reading state is the user's, and it is central.** Unread/read is a first-class, user-visible state on every item, with bulk "mark all read" and "keep unread" as standard escapes. The unread count is the primary signal that draws the user back.
- **Items are attributed references.** Content arrives with its source attached; reading in place and reading at the source are both normal, and the link back is never lost.
- **Items are recognized across fetches.** Feed formats carry per-item identifiers precisely so the reader can avoid re-showing an item it has already delivered; this is what makes repeated checking safe.
- **The stream persists independently of the source.** What the reader has received stays readable in the reader even if the source page later changes or the site disappears — within whatever retention the product offers.
- **Subscriptions require maintenance.** Sources go quiet or vanish. The user decides when a silent feed is finished; some products surface stale feeds and delivery errors to support that judgment, and deletion of dead subscriptions is a normal act, not an exceptional one.
- **Saved ≠ unread.** The starred/bookmarked layer deliberately separates "worth keeping" from "not yet consumed"; marking read and keeping are independent acts.
definition.rules_zh:
- **列表是选择器。** 阅读器展示用户订阅所交付的内容——没有编辑选择，没有算法插入未请求的项目。产品在这个核心周围的可选附加功能有所不同，但信息流本身是用户列表的实体化。这是阅读器与聚合器之间的结构性界限。
- **阅读状态属于用户，且处于核心地位。** 未读/已读是每个项目上一流的、用户可见的状态，带有批量“全部标记为已读”和“保持未读”作为标准逃生机制。未读计数是吸引用户回来的主要信号。
- **项目是带归属的引用。** 内容到达时附带其来源；就地阅读和在来源处阅读都是正常的，且返回链接永远不会丢失。
- **项目在多次获取中被识别。** Feed 格式携带每个项目的标识符，正是为了让阅读器能够避免重复展示已交付的项目；这使得重复检查变得安全。
- **信息流独立于来源而持久存在。** 阅读器已接收的内容即使来源页面后来改变或网站消失，在阅读器中仍然可读——在产品提供的保留期限内。
- **订阅需要维护。** 来源会沉默或消失。用户决定一个沉默的 Feed 何时结束；一些产品展示陈旧 Feed 和交付错误以支持这一判断，删除死订阅是一个正常操作，而非例外操作。
- **已保存 ≠ 未读。** 星标/书签层刻意将“值得保留”与“尚未消费”分开；标记已读和保留是独立的动作。

definition.name: Academic Paper Reader
definition.overview:
An **Academic Paper Reader** is an application for reading scholarly articles. Its world is a persistent library of identified papers, and its primary interaction is reading a paper's full published content on a dedicated reading surface that is built for scholarly work — annotation, navigation by the paper's structure, and keeping the reader's notes attached to the paper.

The defining structure is small:

```text
Scholarly Paper Record (document content + bibliographic identity)
└── held in a Persistent Library
    └── Reading Surface for the paper's full published content
```

What makes this distinct from opening a PDF in a viewer is that a paper here is not an anonymous file: the document is bound to its bibliographic identity (authors, venue, year, or a scholarly identifier such as a DOI or arXiv ID), and papers accumulate across sessions in a durable, organized collection. Everything else commonly associated with these products — import machinery, tags and folders, cross-device sync, AI summaries and chat, sharing — is standard or optional structure layered on that core.
definition.overview_zh:
一个**学术论文阅读器**是用于阅读学术文章的应用程序。其世界是一个由已识别论文构成的持久化图书馆，其主要交互是在一个专为学术工作打造的专用阅读界面上阅读论文的完整已发表内容——包括批注、按论文结构导航，以及将读者的笔记附着在论文上。

其定义性结构很小：

```text
学术论文记录（文档内容 + 书目身份）
└── 存储于持久化图书馆中
     └── 用于论文完整已发表内容的阅读界面
```

使其区别于在查看器中打开 PDF 之处在于，这里的论文并非匿名文件：文档与其书目身份（作者、发表场所、年份，或如 DOI 或 arXiv ID 等学术标识符）绑定，并且论文会在跨会话的持久、有序集合中累积。通常与这些产品关联的其他所有内容——导入机制、标签和文件夹、跨设备同步、AI 摘要和聊天、共享——都是叠加在该核心之上的标准或可选结构。
definition.dc:
```text
Scholarly Paper Record
└── Persistent Library
    └── Reading Surface
```

Three properties. If any one is removed, the product stops being recognizable as an academic paper reader:

- **Scholarly paper as an identified record** — the central object is a paper: the document's content held together with its bibliographic identity. The identity is what makes papers addressable, comparable, and citable across the library. In practice the content is usually a PDF, sometimes with supplementary files attached. If the document is just a file without identity, the product is a generic document viewer.
- **Persistent library** — papers are held over time as the reader's working collection, organized and returned to across sessions. This is a library, not an inbox to be cleared. If nothing is held, the product is a viewer or a one-shot question-answering tool.
- **Reading surface for the full published content** — the primary act is reading the paper itself as published: full text in its fixed layout, with figures, tables, equations, and the reference list in place. Not a summary, a snippet feed, or an answer panel. If the held document disappears and only corpus-level answers remain, the product is a search or answering tool.
definition.dc_zh:
学术论文记录
└── 持久库
    └── 阅读界面
definition.rules:
- **Identity precedes organization.** An imported file without a matching bibliographic record is treated as incomplete: most products will attempt to identify it automatically and give the reader repair paths (identifier lookup, attaching it to an existing record, manual entry) when the match fails.
- **Annotations are attached to the paper, not just to a session.** They persist, remain anchored to their location in the document, and are expected to survive sync and re-reading.
- **Storage of annotations varies.** In some products annotations live in the application's own data rather than inside the PDF file, so they may not be visible if the same file is opened in a different viewer; some products can write annotations into an exported copy of the file.
- **File-structure changes can detach annotations.** Reordering, deleting, or rotating pages outside the product can make page-anchored annotations point to the wrong place; this is why some readers offer their own page-management or warn against structural edits elsewhere.
- **The library is durable by design.** In deliberate contrast with read-it-later tools, papers are not expected to be "processed and cleared"; retention is the normal case.
- **Augmentation is corpus- and license-dependent.** Where products add AI features (summaries, in-context citation details, chat), they may apply only to papers available in the provider's index or where the publisher's terms allow it; availability can vary from paper to paper.
definition.rules_zh:
- **身份先于组织。** 没有匹配书目记录的导入文件被视为不完整：大多数产品会尝试自动识别它，并在匹配失败时提供修复路径（标识符查找、将其附加到现有记录、手动输入）。
- **批注附着在论文上，而不仅仅是在会话中。** 它们持久存在，保持锚定在文档中的位置，并预期在同步和重读后依然存活。
- **批注的存储方式各异。** 在某些产品中，批注存储于应用自身的数据中，而非 PDF 文件内部，因此如果在不同的查看器中打开同一文件，可能无法看到它们；某些产品可以将批注写入文件的导出副本中。
- **文件结构变更可能导致批注脱离。** 在产品外部重新排序、删除或旋转页面可能会使基于页面的批注指向错误位置；这就是为什么某些阅读器提供自己的页面管理或警告在其他地方进行结构编辑的原因。
- **图书馆在设计上是持久的。** 与稍后阅读工具形成刻意对比，论文不被期望被“处理并清除”；保留是常态。
- **增强功能依赖于语料库和许可。** 当产品添加 AI 功能（摘要、上下文引用详情、聊天）时，它们可能仅适用于提供商索引中可用的论文，或出版商条款允许的情况；可用性可能因论文而异。

definition.name: E-book Library Application
definition.overview:
An **E-book Library Application** manages a collection of e-books as a *library*: it keeps a persistent catalog of book entries, each entry holding the book's file(s), its metadata, and its cover; it organizes that catalog by book attributes (collections, tags, series, search); and it provides read access to every entry — through a reader built into the product, by handing the book off to another reading surface, or by delivering it to a device or reading client.

The defining structure is small:

```text
Acquisition (import / scan / purchase)
→ Library entry (book record: file(s) + metadata + cover)
    → organized by book attributes (collections / tags / series / search)
    → read access (built-in reader · external handoff · device or client delivery)
```

Everything else commonly associated with the category — format conversion, device syncing, reading-progress tracking, want-to-read lists, cloud sync, stores, multi-user sharing, DRM handling — is widespread in current products but is not part of what makes the application a library. Removing the collection yields a plain book viewer; removing the book-level organization yields a file manager; removing read access yields a mere catalog. The type lives between those three.
definition.overview_zh:
一个**电子书库应用程序**将一组电子书作为*图书馆*进行管理：它维护一个持久的图书条目目录，每个条目包含该书的文件、元数据及封面；它根据图书属性（合集、标签、系列、搜索）对该目录进行组织；并为每个条目提供阅读访问——通过产品内置的阅读器、将图书转交给其他阅读界面，或将其交付到设备或阅读客户端。

其定义性结构很小：

```text
获取（导入 / 扫描 / 购买）
→ 图书馆条目（图书记录：文件 + 元数据 + 封面）
     → 按图书属性组织（合集 / 标签 / 系列 / 搜索）
     → 阅读访问（内置阅读器 · 外部转交 · 设备或客户端交付）
```

通常与该类别相关的其他一切——格式转换、设备同步、阅读进度跟踪、想读列表、云同步、商店、多用户共享、DRM 处理——在当前产品中很普遍，但并非使该应用程序成为图书馆的本质部分。移除集合将得到一个普通的图书查看器；移除图书级组织将得到一个文件管理器；移除阅读访问将得到一个纯粹的目录。该类型存在于这三者之间。
definition.dc:
```text
Library entry (book record)
├── file(s) — one or more formats of the same work
├── metadata — title, author, cover, and beyond
├── organization — collections / tags / series / search over book attributes
└── read access — built-in reader, external handoff, or delivery to a reading client
```

Three properties. If any one is removed, the product is no longer recognizable as an e-book library:

- **A persistent collection of book entries.** The unit inside the application is a *book* — one entry per work — not a file. An entry aggregates everything the application knows about that work and survives across sessions. Without the persistent collection, the product is just a viewer opened ad hoc on a file.
- **Book-level identity and organization.** Each entry is identified as a book (title and author are its face, the cover its thumbnail) and can be grouped, filtered, and located by book attributes — not by file attributes. Without this, the product is a file manager that happens to contain books.
- **Read access for every entry.** The library exists so the books can be read. Reading may happen inside the product's own reader, in another application the book is handed to, or on a device or client the book is delivered to. Without any path to reading, the product is a bibliographic catalog, not a working library.
definition.dc_zh:
库条目（书籍记录）
├── 文件 — 同一作品的一种或多种格式
├── 元数据 — 标题、作者、封面及其他信息
├── 组织 — 收藏/标签/系列/基于书籍属性的搜索
└── 阅读访问 — 内置阅读器、外部传递或投递到阅读客户端

三个属性。移除任何一个，该产品将不再能被识别为电子书库：

- **一个持久的书籍条目集合。** 应用程序内的单位是书籍——每个作品一个条目——而非文件。条目聚合了应用程序关于该作品的所有信息，并跨会话持续存在。没有这个持久集合，产品只是一个临时打开文件的查看器。
- **书籍级别的身份和组织。** 每个条目被识别为一本书（标题和作者是其面孔，封面是其缩略图），并且可以按书籍属性进行分组、过滤和定位——而非文件属性。没有这个，产品是一个恰好包含书籍的文件管理器。
- **每个条目的阅读访问。** 库的存在是为了让书籍可以被阅读。阅读可以在产品自己的阅读器中进行，在书被传递到的另一个应用程序中进行，或在书被投递到的设备或客户端上进行。没有任何阅读路径，产品是一个书目目录，而非一个工作的库。
definition.rules:
### The library is a layer over the books, distinct from the raw files

A library's catalog is data about works, held separately from whatever files hold the text. Some desktop library managers make this explicit by keeping their own managed copies — the user's original files stay untouched while the library builds its catalog around copies — which makes the library safe to restructure (re-organize, re-format, re-export) without risking the source files. Where a library does hold the only copy (store purchases, server-scanned folders), the library's storage *is* the book's home, and backup behavior matters.

### One entry, many formats

The same work in several formats is commonly held as one entry carrying several files, not as several entries. This is where the distinction between books and files has teeth: the entry is the unit of meaning; formats are its contents. Library managers commonly allow the user to remove or add individual formats without touching the entry.

### Removal separates the catalog from the files — or doesn't

What "remove a book" means varies: deleting the entry and its files permanently, removing only one format, emptying the entry to metadata-only, or removing the entry while keeping the files. Whether a removal can be undone also varies by product. A reader should treat removal as the library's most destructive ordinary action.

### Rights management constrains what a library can do

For store-acquired or otherwise protected books, the library's abilities may be limited by rights management: conversion may be refused, transfer restricted, and some protected formats may be readable only in the vendor's designated application, with the library acting as the shelf and launcher rather than the reader. A library that handles only DRM-free files has no such constraints; the pattern, not the specifics, is the type-level rule.

### Automated metadata is a starting point, not a truth

Metadata arrives imperfect — derived from file names that mislead, embedded data that is missing, or store records that differ between editions. Every mature library therefore exposes metadata as editable, and correction is a normal, expected activity rather than an exception.

### Reading handoff is format- and product-dependent

Not every entry is read in the product's own reader. Some formats are deliberately opened by another application; some books travel to devices or remote clients. What must hold is that a path to reading exists; which path is used is a per-format, per-product decision.

### In shared libraries, state belongs to the reader

Where a library is served to multiple users, the collection is shared while the reading experience is not: each user brings their own progress, bookmarks, and restrictions, while the underlying entries are common. Access control operates at library and entry level, and age or content-rating restrictions may govern visibility per user.
definition.rules_zh:
### 图书馆是图书之上的一层，与原始文件不同

图书馆的目录是关于作品的数据，与承载文本的文件分开保存。一些桌面图书馆管理器通过保留自己管理的副本使这一点明确——用户的原始文件保持不动，而图书馆围绕副本构建其目录——这使得图书馆可以安全地重构（重新组织、重新格式化、重新导出）而不冒源文件的风险。当图书馆持有唯一副本时（商店购买、服务器扫描的文件夹），图书馆的存储*就是*图书的家园，备份行为很重要。

### 一个条目，多种格式

同一部作品的多种格式通常作为携带多个文件的一个条目保存，而不是作为多个条目。这是图书与文件之间区别的关键所在：条目是意义单元；格式是其内容。图书馆管理器通常允许用户在不触及条目的情况下移除或添加单个格式。

definition.name: E-book Reader
definition.overview:
An **E-book Reader** is an application that turns a digital book into a reading experience: it opens one book at a time, presents the book's content for sustained reading on screen, keeps track of where the reader is in each book, and moves the reader through the book — page by page or scroll by scroll, with navigation back into any part of it.

The defining core is deliberately small:

```text
The opened book
└── Reading-oriented presentation (paginated or flowing, adapted to the screen)
    └── Persistent per-book reading position
        └── In-book movement (page turns / scrolling, resumed where you left off)
```

Everything else commonly associated with modern reading apps — typography panels, night themes, highlights and notes, dictionaries, read-aloud, bookshelves, store purchase, cloud sync, DRM handling — is widespread in current products but is machinery around the core, not the core. Older and simpler reading applications (desktop and PDA-era readers, plain-text book readers on early phones) satisfy the same core with none of those features.

When the center of gravity shifts from the reading session to the collection of books — acquiring, organizing, cataloging and delivering them — the product is drifting toward a different Application Type (E-book Library Application).
definition.overview_zh:
一款**电子书阅读器**是一种将数字书籍转化为阅读体验的应用程序：它一次打开一本书，在屏幕上呈现书籍内容以供持续阅读，记录读者在每本书中的位置，并引导读者在书中移动——逐页翻页或逐段滚动，并可导航回书中的任何部分。

其定义性核心被刻意保持精简：

```text
已打开的书籍
└── 面向阅读的内容呈现（分页或流式，适配屏幕）
     └── 每本书的持久化阅读位置
         └── 书内移动（翻页/滚动，从上次停止处继续）
```

现代阅读应用中常见的其他功能——排版面板、夜间主题、高亮与笔记、词典、朗读、书架、商店购买、云同步、DRM 处理——在当前产品中虽已普及，但它们只是围绕核心的机械组件，而非核心本身。更早期、更简单的阅读应用（桌面端及 PDA 时代的阅读器、早期手机上的纯文本书籍阅读器）在没有任何上述功能的情况下，同样满足这一核心需求。

当产品的重心从阅读会话转移到书籍集合——获取、组织、编目和交付书籍——时，该产品便正在向另一种应用类型（电子书库应用）漂移。
definition.dc:
```text
The opened book
└── Reading-oriented presentation
    └── Persistent per-book reading position
        └── In-book movement
```

Four properties. If any one is removed, the product is no longer recognizable as an e-book reader:

- **The opened book** — one digital book document is loaded into a reading surface at a time. The reading session is the unit of work; the reader's world is the book in hand, not the collection of books. Without this, the product is a library or catalog.
- **Reading-oriented presentation** — the book's content is laid out for sustained reading: paginated text, or continuously flowing text, adapted to the screen. It is never raw file contents, and it is not an editing surface. Without this, the product is a file viewer or text editor.
- **Persistent per-book reading position** — where the reader is in each book is first-class state that survives closing the application. Reopening resumes the book. Without this, long-form reading across sessions collapses, and the product degrades into a static renderer.
- **In-book movement** — the primary interaction is advancing through the book from that position: page turns or scrolling, plus the ability to move back and forth. Without movement, there is no reading flow.
definition.dc_zh:
已打开的书
└── 面向阅读的呈现
    └── 每本书的持久阅读位置
        └── 书中移动
definition.rules:
### Position persistence is the defining behavior

The reader's central state is the per-book position. It advances while reading, survives closing the application, and is the anchor that "continue reading" surfaces restore. Products that sync extend this state across devices; products that don't keep it local. Either way, the position belongs to the book, not to the device session.

### The reflow rule

This is the load-bearing structural rule of the Type. For **reflowable** books, the reader's typographic choices re-lay-out and re-paginate the text: enlarging the font increases the page count, and a highlight made "on page 38" may land on a different screen page after an adjustment. Visual page numbers in a reflowable book are therefore unstable — which is why position state must be text-anchored, and why products offer **print-equivalent page numbers** (publisher-embedded print pagination) when citations must match the paper edition. For **fixed-layout** content (PDF, comics, fixed-layout epubs), the text cannot re-flow: comfort controls degrade to zoom, crop, and theme, and page numbers are stable by construction. Mature readers handle both poles, but the two poles behave differently under every control.

### Annotations attach to text, not to visual pages

Because of the reflow rule, highlights and notes bind to locations in the book's text so they survive re-layout and device changes. Some products can additionally write annotations into the document itself (a fixed-layout specialty) or export them in standard formats.

### License can gate the book

For store-licensed content, the license — not the file — determines readability: opening may require account authorization, and borrowed titles can expire and remove access. The reader surface itself is indifferent to where the file came from; the license layer sits in front of it in store-based families.

### Reading aids overlay the page

Menus, dictionaries, translation pop-ups, and statistics are overlays and side panels. The reading page remains the durable surface; aids appear over it and disappear, and the reading position is never disturbed by using them.

### Settings follow the book

Appearance choices are remembered per book (with global defaults in many products), so a re-opened book returns in the shape the reader left it — an application of the same persistence logic that governs position.
definition.rules_zh:
### 位置持久化是定义性行为

读者的核心状态是每本书的位置。它在阅读过程中前进，在关闭应用后依然保留，并且是“继续阅读”界面恢复的锚点。支持同步的产品将此状态扩展到跨设备；不支持同步的产品则将其保留在本地。无论哪种方式，位置属于书籍，而非设备会话。

### 重排规则

这是该类型的承重结构规则。对于**可重排**书籍，读者的排版选择会重新排版并重新分页文本：增大字体会增加页数，在“第 38 页”做的高亮在调整后可能落在不同的屏幕页上。因此，可重排书籍中的视觉页码是不稳定的——这就是为什么位置状态必须基于文本锚定，以及为什么产品在需要引用匹配纸质版时提供**印刷等效页码**（出版商嵌入的印刷分页）。对于**固定版式**内容（PDF、漫画、固定版式 epub），文本无法重排：舒适度控件退化为缩放、裁剪和主题，页码在结构上是稳定的。成熟的阅读器能处理这两个极端，但这两个极端在每种控件下的表现不同。

### 注释绑定到文本，而非视觉页面

由于重排规则，高亮和笔记绑定到书籍文本中的位置，以便在重新排版和设备变更后依然有效。部分产品还可以将注释写入文档本身（固定版式的特色）或以标准格式导出。
