definition.name: PDF / Document Reader
definition.overview:
A **PDF / Document Reader** is an application for reading document files produced elsewhere: it opens a whole document — regardless of subject matter or origin — renders its pages faithfully in the layout the file defines, and lets the reader move through the document and interact with its content without changing what the document *is*.

The defining core is small:

```text
Document file from an external source
└── Faithful fixed-layout page rendering
    └── Movement through the paginated document
        (paging, jumping, scale adjustment)
```

Everything else commonly associated with PDF applications — annotation, form filling, digital signatures, text search, page reorganization, enterprise security tooling, AI assistance — is widespread in current products but is not what makes the product a document reader. The Type's historical root is the plain read-only viewer, and a viewer with none of the modern machinery remains fully inside the Type.

When the center of gravity shifts — re-laying-out content for reading comfort, authoring or editing the document's content, curating a collection of books or papers — the product has drifted toward a different Application Type (E-book Reader, Document Editor, E-book Library, Academic Paper Reader).
definition.overview_zh:
一款 **PDF / 文档阅读器** 是用于阅读在其他地方生成的文档文件的应用程序：它打开整个文档——无论主题或来源如何——按照文件定义的布局忠实地渲染其页面，并允许读者在文档中移动并与内容交互，而不改变文档*本身*的性质。

其定义性核心很小：

```text
来自外部源的文档文件
└── 忠实的固定布局页面渲染
     └── 在分页文档中的移动
         （翻页、跳转、缩放调整）
```

通常与 PDF 应用程序相关联的其他一切——注释、表单填写、数字签名、文本搜索、页面重组、企业安全工具、AI 辅助——在当前产品中很普遍，但这并不是使该产品成为文档阅读器的原因。该类型的历史根源是纯只读查看器，一个没有现代机制的查看器仍然完全属于该类型。

当重心转移——为阅读舒适度重新布局内容、创作或编辑文档内容、整理书籍或论文集合——该产品已偏离到不同的应用程序类型（电子书阅读器、文档编辑器、电子书库、学术论文阅读器）。
definition.dc:
```text
Document file from an external source
└── Faithful fixed-layout page rendering
    └── Movement through the paginated document
        (paging, jumping, scale adjustment)
```

Three properties. If any one is removed, the product is no longer recognizable as a document reader:

- **The externally-obtained document as the unit of reading.** The application opens whole document files of arbitrary provenance and content — invoices, manuals, papers, forms, brochures. It holds no authoring relationship to the content and no collection semantics of its own. Without this, the product is an authoring tool or a content service, not a reader.
- **Faithful fixed-layout page rendering.** Pages are presented as fixed compositions — text, images, and graphics placed at exact positions, with pagination determined by the file itself. The same file looks the same everywhere; the application's obligation is fidelity to the file as authored, not re-presentation for comfort. Without this, the product re-lays-out content (e-book reader) or changes content (editor).
- **Movement through the paginated document.** Because the layout is fixed and does not adapt to the window, reading requires machinery to move: scrolling and paging between pages, jumping to a page or position, and adjusting viewing scale (zoom, fit-to-window/page/width). Without this, the product is a static page image.
definition.dc_zh:
来自外部源的文档文件
└── 忠实的固定布局页面渲染
    └── 在分页文档中移动
        (翻页、跳转、缩放调整)
definition.rules:
### Fidelity is the obligation

The reader renders what the file says. It does not re-flow text to fit the window, does not re-typeface for comfort, does not "improve" the layout. Everything that changes presentation rather than scale belongs to other Types. This is the structural contrast with e-book reading, where the presentation is the app's to optimize.

### The text layer is not guaranteed

A PDF's pages may be true text or may be scanned images. When there is no text layer, search, selection, and copy do not work — a failure mode documented in mainstream products' own troubleshooting guides. Text recognition features in some products exist precisely to bridge this gap; the base behavior is: **no text layer, no text interaction**.

### Documents carry permissions; readers enforce them

An author can protect a document: a password to open it, and restrictions on printing or copying content. The reader enforces these — it can refuse to print a restricted document or require a password before text can be copied. The reader never grants rights the file does not carry.

### Markup and form data are changes to a copy

Annotation and form input modify the opened document (or a copy of it). Persistence mechanics differ — some products write back into the file, some require an explicit save-as-copy step — but in all cases unsaved work is transient. A filled form that is not saved is lost.

### The outline is the document's, not the app's

A table of contents exists only if the authoring tool put one in the file. Most documents carry none; the reader must remain fully usable through thumbnails, page numbers, and search alone.

### The file is live

The reader views a file that other programs may change while it is open; products commonly reload the document when the file changes underneath. The reader is a window onto the file, not a container that owns it.

### Reading is not editing

The line the market itself maintains: readers present, mark up, fill, and sign; they do not rewrite the document's content. Products that do both split the capability into a separate editor product or explicitly disclaim editing. Page-level organization (combining, reordering, deleting pages) is the gray zone — offered by some readers as a convenience, owned by editors as a job — and is treated here as optional, never defining.
definition.rules_zh:
### 保真度是义务

阅读器渲染文件所说的内容。它不重新流动文本以适应窗口，不为舒适度重新排版，不“改进”布局。所有改变呈现而非比例的内容属于其他类型。这与电子书阅读形成结构性对比，在电子书阅读中，呈现是应用程序要优化的。

### 文本层不是保证的

PDF 的页面可能是真正的文本，也可能是扫描图像。当没有文本层时，搜索、选择和复制不起作用——这是主流产品自己的故障排除指南中记录的故障模式。某些产品中的文本识别功能正是为了弥合这一差距；基本行为是：**没有文本层，就没有文本交互**。

### 文档携带权限；阅读器执行它们

作者可以保护文档：打开它的密码，以及对打印或复制内容的限制。阅读器执行这些——它可以拒绝打印受限制的文档，或在复制文本前要求密码。阅读器从不授予文件不携带的权利。

### 标记和表单数据是对副本的更改

注释和表单输入修改打开的文档（或其副本）。持久化机制不同——一些产品写回文件，一些需要显式的另存为副本步骤——但在所有情况下，未保存的工作是暂时的。未保存的已填写表单会丢失。

### 大纲属于文档，不属于应用程序

只有当创作工具在文件中放入目录时，目录才存在。大多数文档没有；阅读器必须仅通过缩略图、页码和搜索保持完全可用。

### 文件是活动的

阅读器查看的文件可能在打开时被其他程序更改；产品通常在文件更改时重新加载文档

definition.name: Read-it-later Application
definition.overview:
A **Read-it-later Application** is a personal reading application built around a queue: it captures content the user encounters but does not want to read in that moment — web articles above all, and at the modern pole PDFs, e-books, videos, and newsletters — holds each saved item together with a copy of its content, presents that content itself for in-app reading at a later time, and retires items from the queue once they have been read.

The defining core is small:

```text
Deliberate capture (a save act performed from elsewhere)
└── Saved reading item — source link + held content
    └── Deferred-reading queue — unread → read → archived/removed
        └── In-app reading surface — the product presents the content itself
```

Everything else commonly associated with the category — reader-mode extraction, offline caching, cross-device sync, tags, highlights, text-to-speech, AI assistance — is standard in mature modern products or common variants, but is not what makes the product a read-it-later application. The platform-native form (a browser's built-in reading list) satisfies the core with none of those extras.

When the product stops clearing items — when retention becomes the normal case rather than the exception — it is drifting toward a reading library. When it hands the user an organized address instead of the content, it is a bookmark manager. When intake is dominated by subscription streams rather than deliberate saves, it is drifting toward a feed reader.
definition.overview_zh:
一款**稍后阅读应用**是围绕队列构建的个人阅读应用：它捕获用户遇到但当下不想阅读的内容——主要是网络文章，在当代语境下还包括PDF、电子书、视频和新闻通讯——将每个保存的项目与其内容副本一起保留，在稍后时间于应用内呈现该内容以供阅读，并在阅读完成后将项目从队列中移除。

其定义性核心很小：

```text
刻意捕获（从其他地方执行的保存操作）
└── 已保存的阅读项目——源链接 + 保留的内容
     └── 延迟阅读队列——未读 → 已读 → 归档/移除
         └── 应用内阅读界面——产品呈现内容本身
```

通常与该类别关联的其他一切——阅读模式提取、离线缓存、跨设备同步、标签、高亮、文本转语音、AI辅助——在成熟的现代产品中是标准配置或常见变体，但这并非使产品成为稍后阅读应用的原因。平台原生形式（浏览器内置的阅读列表）在没有任何这些额外功能的情况下即可满足核心需求。

当产品停止清理项目——当保留成为常态而非例外——它正在向阅读库漂移。当它向用户提供组织好的地址而非内容本身时，它就是一个书签管理器。当摄入主要由订阅流而非刻意保存主导时，它正在向订阅源阅读器漂移。
definition.dc:
Three jointly-held structures. Remove any one and the product stops being recognizable as this Type.

**1. The saved reading item as the unit of record.**
A persistent, individually addressable entry in the user's library, created by a deliberate save act performed somewhere else — a browser page, a share sheet, a paste, an email. Each item carries, at minimum, its source (title and origin link) and its content in a form the product can present for reading: commonly an extracted, cleaned reading copy; an archived copy of the original page; an uploaded document such as a PDF or e-book; or media with its transcript. The content is the working object — this is what separates the Type from a bookmark, which holds an organized address and leaves the content on the web. The origin link stays with the item: when the held copy is wrong or incomplete, the link is the fallback and the way back to the source.

**2. The deferred-reading queue posture.**
The collection is lived in as a queue of things to read *later*. New items enter unread; the primary surfaces sort and filter by reading state; and items are *consumed* — marked read and set aside (archived, removed, or deleted) once handled. Keeping an item is the deliberate exception, expressed as a favorites/starred layer, not the default fate of every save. The queue's health is measured by items being processed and cleared, not by the library growing. This posture is what separates the Type from a permanent library (nothing is "later" there, and nothing is expected to leave) and from a feed (where the source, not the user's intent, drives what arrives).

**3. The in-app reading surface as the product's main act.**
The product itself presents the saved content for reading — a typographic reader-mode view for articles, an archived-page view, a document viewer for PDFs and e-books, a player or transcript view for media. Reading-comfort controls (typography, themes, layout) surround the content. The alternative — handing the user back out to the open web — is a link list, not a reading application.
definition.dc_zh:
三个共同持有的结构。移除任何一个，产品就不再是此类型。

**1. 保存的阅读项目作为记录单位。**
一个持久的、可单独寻址的用户库条目，通过在其他地方执行的故意保存操作创建——如浏览器页面、分享菜单、粘贴或电子邮件。每个项目至少包含其来源（标题和原始链接）和产品可呈现以供阅读的内容形式：通常是提取的、清理过的阅读副本；原始页面的存档副本；上传的文档如PDF或电子书；或带有其转录的媒体。内容是工作对象——这将该类型与书签区分开来，书签持有组织化的地址并将内容留在网络上。原始链接保留在项目上：当保存的副本错误或不完整时，链接是后备并返回到源的方式。

**2. 延迟阅读队列姿态。**
集合被作为稍后阅读的队列来生活。新项目以未读状态进入；主要界面按阅读状态排序和过滤；并且项目被*消费*——一旦处理就标记为已读并搁置（归档、移除或删除）。保留项目是故意的例外，表达为收藏/星标层，而不是每次保存的默认命运。队列的健康度通过处理和清除的项目来衡量，而不是通过
definition.rules:
### Save is not read

Saving deliberately does not mark anything read. The unseen state persists until the user actually opens the item — this is the queue's honesty, and products surface it visibly (unread counts, unseen markers that disappear on open).

### The held copy can be wrong; the link is the fallback

Extraction is an automated interpretation of someone else's page, and it fails: paywalled content, scraping blocks, fragile layouts. Mature products treat this as a designed-for case — re-fetch, per-site parsing rules, rendered-content fallbacks — and always keep the origin link on the item. The queue may degrade to a link for a broken item, but degradation is the exception the product works to repair, not the design center.

### Archive is not delete

The post-consumption state is distinct from removal. Archived items leave the attention stream but remain retrievable; deletion (with trash/restore where offered) is the irreversible act. The platform-native minimal form collapses this layering to "hide what you've read" — the state distinction is maturity, not invariant.

### The queue is private by default

The library is a personal space. Sharing, where it exists at all, is an explicit act (sending an item onward, publishing a highlighted passage), never the ambient state of the collection.

### The library outlives the service (or should)

Data portability — export of items, states, and annotations in open formats — is a structural expectation of the category, born of repeated shutdowns. It is the user's hedge against the queue being their only copy of things they meant to read.
definition.rules_zh:
### 保存不等于阅读

保存刻意不标记任何内容为已读。未看状态持续存在，直到用户实际打开该项目——这是队列的诚实性，产品会将其可视化呈现（未读计数、在打开时消失的未看标记）。

### 保留的副本可能出错；链接是后备

提取是对他人页面的自动化解释，它会失败：付费内容、抓取封锁、脆弱布局。成熟产品将此视为设计好的情况——重新获取、逐站点解析规则、渲染内容后备——并始终在项目中保留源链接。队列对于损坏的项目可能降级为链接，但降级是产品努力修复的例外，而非设计中心。

### 归档不等于删除

消费后状态与移除不同。归档项目离开注意力流但仍可检索；删除（在提供时带有回收站/恢复）是不可逆操作。平台原生最小形式将此分层折叠为“隐藏已读内容”——状态区分是成熟度，而非不变量。

### 队列默认是私有的

库是个人空间。共享，如果存在，是明确的操作（将项目转发、发布高亮段落），而非集合的环境状态。

### 库比服务更持久（或应该如此）

数据可移植性——以开放格式导出项目、状态和注释——是该类别的结构预期，源于反复的关闭。它是用户对冲队列成为其想读内容唯一副本的手段。

definition.name: Public Data Portal
definition.overview:
A **Public Data Portal** is a publication platform through which an organization makes collections of data available to the general public as **datasets** — each held as a persistent, metadata-described record to which the data itself is attached as downloadable files or queryable APIs. The public discovers data through an open catalog (search and browse), evaluates each dataset from its record (what it contains, who published it, what it covers, how current it is, how it may be used), and takes the data away for its own purposes.

The defining core is small:

```text
Maintained dataset record (metadata-described, the portal's own catalog content)
└── Data distributions (files and/or APIs attached to the record)
    └── Public discovery surface (open search/browse over the whole corpus)
        └── Public-access posture (published once for all comers, under recorded terms)
```

Everything commonly associated with modern portals — in-browser charts and maps, query APIs with developer documentation, publisher workspaces, update automation, usage analytics — is widespread in current products but is not what makes a portal a portal. Simple table-first statistical services, early-generation catalogs, and small single-publisher download sites satisfy the same definition. The operator can be any body — a government (the specialized case documented separately), an international organization, a statistical agency, a research institution, or an open community.
definition.overview_zh:
一个**公共数据门户**是一个发布平台，组织通过它向公众提供数据集合，作为**数据集**——每个数据集都作为一条持久且带有元数据描述的记录保存，数据本身以可下载文件或可查询 API 的形式附着于该记录。公众通过开放目录（搜索与浏览）发现数据，根据记录评估每个数据集（其包含内容、发布者、覆盖范围、时效性、使用方式），并将数据取走用于自身目的。

其定义性核心很小：

```text
维护的数据集记录（带元数据描述，属于门户自身的目录内容）
└── 数据分发形式（附着于记录的文件和/或 API）
     └── 公共发现界面（覆盖整个语料的开放搜索/浏览）
         └── 公共访问姿态（面向所有来者一次性发布，遵循已记录的条件）
```

现代门户通常关联的一切——浏览器内图表与地图、带开发者文档的查询 API、发布者工作区、更新自动化、使用分析——在当前产品中虽已普及，但并非使门户成为门户的本质。简单的表格优先统计服务、早期目录以及小型单发布者下载站点同样满足此定义。运营方可以是任何机构——政府（作为单独记录的特例）、国际组织、统计机构、研究机构或开放社区。
definition.dc:
- **The public discovery surface.** A search and browse layer over the whole corpus — free-text search, browse listings by topic, publisher, geography, or format — open to anyone, with no need to know in advance which organization holds what and, in the typical case, no account required. Without this, the product is an internal records tool or a private data service.
- **The public-access posture.** The corpus is published **once, for all comers**: acquiring data is governed by the usage terms or license recorded on or alongside the dataset, not by per-consumer grants, subscriptions, or entitlement decisions. Reuse conditions ride with the data; admission to the corpus does not depend on who is asking. Without this, the product drifts toward subscription data services and data-exchange territory.
definition.dc_zh:
- **公共发现界面。** 一个搜索和浏览层，覆盖整个语料库——支持自由文本搜索，按主题、发布者、地理位置或格式浏览列表——对任何人开放，无需事先知道哪个组织持有什么，在典型情况下，无需账户。如果没有这个功能，该产品就是一个内部记录工具或私有数据服务。
- **公共访问姿态。** 语料库**一次性发布，供所有人使用**：获取数据受数据集上或旁边的用法条款或许可证管理，而非针对每个消费者的授权、订阅或权益决定。重用条件随数据而定；进入语料库不取决于谁在请求。如果没有这个特性，产品会倾向于订阅数据服务和数据交换领域。
definition.rules:
- **Published once, for all comers.** There is no requester relationship and no per-consumer entitlement decision. This is the structural line against data-sharing products that mediate access party by party, and against subscription statistics services.
- **Records are maintained, not crawled.** The catalog's entries are the operator's own curated content — even when aggregated from many sources. A service that only indexes third-party data pages is a search engine, not a portal.
- **Terms ride with the data.** Usage conditions are recorded on the dataset or alongside it; their granularity varies (per-record licenses, site-level conditions, per-dataset terms), but the consumer can always see what reuse allows before acquiring.
- **Freshness is declared, not guaranteed.** Update dates and frequencies are metadata; whether a dataset is mechanically refreshed or manually updated varies by dataset and by operator.
- **The portal delivers; it does not own the data of record.** Published datasets are copies, exports, or live views of data whose authoritative versions live in source systems — statistical systems, administrative registers, survey programs.
- **Anonymous by default.** Discovery and download typically require no account; accounts exist for publishing and engagement, not for admission to the corpus.
definition.rules_zh:
- **一次性发布，面向所有来者。** 不存在请求者关系，也不存在针对每个消费者的授权决策。这是与逐方中介访问的数据共享产品以及订阅制统计服务之间的结构性分界线。
- **记录是维护的，而非爬取的。** 目录条目是运营方自身策划的内容——即使是从多个来源聚合而来。仅索引第三方数据页面的服务是搜索引擎，而非门户。
- **条款随数据同行。** 使用条件记录在数据集上或其旁侧；其粒度各异（逐记录许可、站点级条件、逐数据集条款），但消费者在获取前总能看清允许何种复用。
- **时效性是被声明的，而非被保证的。** 更新日期与频率属于元数据；数据集是机械刷新还是手动更新，因数据集与运营方而异。
- **门户负责交付，但不拥有权威数据。** 已发布的数据集是副本、导出或实时视图，其权威版本存在于源系统中——统计系统、行政登记册、调查项目。
- **默认匿名。** 发现与下载通常无需账户；账户用于发布与互动，而非用于进入语料库的准入。

definition.name: Bookmark Manager
definition.overview:
A **Bookmark Manager** is a personal library application for the web: it saves references to web resources as durable records, organizes them under the user's control, and makes them findable later so the user can return to those resources.

The defining core is small:

```text
Deliberately saved reference record
└── anchored to an external web resource by its address (URL)
    └── held in a persistent, accumulating personal library
        └── under user-controlled organization
            └── retrieved later to return to the resource
```

Everything else commonly associated with the category — browser extensions, automatic metadata, tags and nested collections, cloud sync, duplicate and broken-link management, preserved copies of pages, public sharing — is standard equipment of mature modern products rather than what makes the product a bookmark manager. Older and platform-native forms of the same idea (a browser's built-in bookmark folders, the tag-only social bookmarking services of the mid-2000s) satisfy the core without any of those features.

The essential job is **save now, find later**. When the center of gravity shifts to consuming captured content (a reading queue), publishing collections for an audience, or storing user-authored material, the product is drifting toward a different Application Type (Read-it-later, Content Curation, or Note-taking respectively).
definition.overview_zh:
一个**书签管理器**是一个用于网络的个人库应用程序：它将指向网络资源的引用保存为持久记录，在用户的控制下进行组织，并使它们日后易于查找，以便用户能够返回这些资源。

其定义性的核心很小：

```text
有意保存的引用记录
└── 通过其地址（URL）锚定到外部网络资源
     └── 存储在一个持久且不断累积的个人库中
         └── 在用户控制的组织之下
             └── 日后检索以返回该资源
```

通常与该类别相关联的其他所有内容——浏览器扩展、自动元数据、标签和嵌套集合、云同步、重复和断链管理、页面的保存副本、公开分享——是成熟现代产品的标准配置，而非使该产品成为书签管理器的原因。同一概念的较旧和平台原生形式（浏览器内置的书签文件夹、2000年代中期的纯标签社交书签服务）在没有这些功能的情况下也能满足核心需求。

基本任务是**现在保存，日后查找**。当重心转移到消费捕获的内容（阅读队列）、为受众发布集合或存储用户创作的材料时，该产品正在向不同的应用程序类型漂移（分别为稍后阅读、内容策展或笔记记录）。
definition.dc:
Four properties. If any one is removed, the product is no longer recognizable as a bookmark manager:

- **Reference record anchored to an address** — the central object is a record that points at a web resource via its URL, enriched with whatever metadata the product adds. The record is not the content; the content lives on the web, outside the library. This is what separates the Type from notes (authored content) and from read-it-later services (the captured readable copy is the working object).
- **Deliberate capture** — every record originates from a user decision to save (a click, a share, a pasted URL, an approved import). Nothing is logged automatically. This is what separates the library from browser history.
- **Persistent, accumulating personal library** — records survive sessions and devices and pile up over time into a long-lived personal asset, often numbering thousands of items.
- **User-controlled organization and retrieval** — the user structures the library in some form and can find records again by browsing that structure and/or by searching. The *form* of organization is an implementation choice, not part of the definition.
definition.dc_zh:
四个属性。如果任何一个被移除，产品将不再被识别为书签管理器：

- **锚定到地址的参考记录** — 中心对象是一个通过URL指向网络资源的记录，可以添加产品添加的任何元数据。记录不是内容；内容存在于网络上，库之外。这将类型与笔记（创作内容）和阅读稍后服务（捕获的可读副本是工作对象）区分开来。

- **故意捕获** — 每个记录都源于用户保存的决定（点击、分享、粘贴的URL、批准的导入）。没有自动记录。这将库与浏览器历史区分开来。

- **持久、积累的个人库** — 记录在会话和设备之间持久存在，并随时间堆积成一个长期的个人资产，通常有数千个项目。

- **用户控制的组织和检索** — 用户以某种形式构建库，并可以通过浏览该结构和/或搜索再次找到记录。组织的形式是实现选择，不是定义的一部分。
definition.rules:
- **The record points; the web owns the content.** A saved page can change or vanish without the record knowing. The library guarantees the *reference*, not the *content* — unless the product also stores a preserved copy, which is an optional capability.
- **The library grows only by user action.** Capture is deliberate. Imports and automated intake (e.g., configured feeds) enlarge the library only because the user set them up. There is no silent accumulation as with browser history.
- **Organization is user-controlled and always revisable.** No structure is imposed by the system; tags and collections mean what the user wants them to mean, and records can be re-filed indefinitely.
- **One resource, generally one record.** Mature products converge on a single record per address — either by preventing duplicates outright or by surfacing them for cleanup — but the strictness varies by product.
- **Private by default.** The library is personal; visibility to others requires an explicit sharing act (a public link, a per-record flag, or an invited member).
- **Deletion is often recoverable, but not always.** Some products hold deleted records in a trash area; others delete permanently, especially in bulk operations.
- **Read-later state, where present, is orthogonal to organization.** A record can be organized and still unread; the unread flag describes the user's relationship to the content, not the record's place in the library.
definition.rules_zh:
- **记录指向；网络拥有内容。** 保存的页面可以在记录不知情的情况下改变或消失。库保证的是*引用*，而非*内容*——除非产品还存储了保存副本，这是一项可选功能。
- **库仅通过用户操作增长。** 捕获是有意为之。导入和自动化接收（例如，配置的源）仅在用户设置它们时才扩大库。不像浏览器历史那样存在静默累积。
- **组织由用户控制且始终可修订。** 系统不施加任何结构；标签和集合意味着用户希望它们意味着的含义，记录可以无限期地重新归档。
- **一个资源，通常一条记录。** 成熟产品趋向于每个地址一条记录——要么直接防止重复，要么将其呈现以供清理——但严格程度因产品而异。
- **默认私有。** 库是个人化的；对他人的可见性需要明确的共享行为（公共链接、逐记录标志或受邀成员）。
- **删除通常可恢复，但并非总是如此。** 某些产品在回收站区域保留已删除的记录；其他产品永久删除，特别是在批量操作中。
- **稍后阅读状态（如果存在）与组织正交。** 记录可以被组织但仍未阅读；未读标志描述的是用户与内容的关系，而非记录在库中的位置。

definition.name: Reading Library Application
definition.overview:
A **Reading Library Application** maintains a person's own library of book records: persistent entries for books the person has read, is reading, wants to read, or owns, organized on shelves or collections the person controls, with each record carrying that reader's relationship to the book — reading state, dates and progress, ownership, ratings, reviews, notes.

The defining core is small:

```text
Book record (bibliographic identity)
└── held in the person's own organized, retained library
    └── carrying that reader's personal relationship to the book
```

What it does **not** hold is the books themselves. A reading library keeps records *about* books — the actual reading happens elsewhere: a physical copy, an e-reader, an audiobook app, a borrowed library book. If the product holds book content and presents it for reading, it has drifted into E-book Library territory; if its entries are links to web pages held for later consumption, it is a Read-it-later or Bookmark Manager.

The type appears in the market under two dominant shapes — the **reading tracker** (organized by reading status: want to read, currently reading, read, did not finish) and the **private library catalog** (organized by possession: what is on my shelves) — both built on the same core.
definition.overview_zh:
一个**阅读图书馆应用**维护个人专属的图书记录库：包含已读、在读、想读或拥有的书籍的持久化条目，这些条目被组织在由用户自行管理的书架或收藏集中，每条记录都承载着读者与该书的关系——阅读状态、日期与进度、所有权、评分、书评、笔记。

其定义性核心非常精简：

```text
图书记录（书目身份）
└── 存放于个人自行组织并保留的图书馆中
     └── 承载该读者与书籍的个人关系
```

它**不**存储书籍本身。阅读图书馆保存的是*关于*书籍的记录——实际阅读发生在别处：实体书、电子阅读器、有声书应用或借阅的图书馆书籍。如果产品存储书籍内容并供阅读，则已偏离至电子图书馆领域；如果其条目是供日后消费的网页链接，则属于稍后阅读或书签管理器。

该类型在市场上呈现两种主导形态——**阅读追踪器**（按阅读状态组织：想读、在读、已读、未完成）和**私人图书馆目录**（按拥有情况组织：书架上有什么）——两者均建立在相同的核心之上。
definition.dc_zh:
**书籍记录。** 单元是所有事物的持久、个体识别的书籍记录——锚定于书目身份：至少标题和作者，通常包括封面图像、版本、出版细节和描述。记录由个人主动添加：通过搜索产品图书目录、导入从另一服务导出的文件、扫描ISBN条码或手动创建条目。记录是被保留的；它既不是网页链接，也不是书籍文件。

**个人图书馆。** 记录存在于个人自己的图书馆中——一个可搜索和浏览的整体，组织成用户管理的组。规范组是*书架*或*收藏集*：个人控制的命名集合。图书馆被保留，而非消耗——已读的书籍保留在记录中，通常终身。这是待读队列的结构对立面，后者会清除已处理项目。

**个人关系层。** 将书籍目录变成*我的*图书馆的是记录读者与每本书关系的数据层。这一层是个人层，不是固定清单——产品以不同方式组合它，借鉴于：- **阅读状态** — 书籍在阅读生活中的位置：想读 / 正在阅读 / 已读，通常还有未完成或停止状态；- **阅读日期和进度** — 书籍被阅读的时间。
definition.rules:
- **Records, not content.** The product never presents the text of the book. Every object in the system is about the book (identity, status, opinion); the reading itself is done elsewhere. This is the type's clearest structural signature.
- **Retention is normal.** Finished books are not cleared; they accumulate. The library's health is measured by its completeness and growth, not by an empty queue.
- **Status is usually exclusive.** In tracker-form products a book typically occupies exactly one reading status at a time — moving forward moves it out of the previous shelf — while custom shelves/collections hold books independently of status. (Documented explicitly in the sampled open-source tracker; treat the exact mechanics as product-dependent.)
- **One shared identity per book.** Because records resolve against a shared catalog, two readers referencing the same book are referencing the same record — which is what makes community reviews and comparisons possible. Users can usually correct catalog data; some products route corrections to staff review.
- **The library is portable.** Export/import is an expected property; the person's library is their data, movable between products (with the caveat that matching old records to a new catalog is approximate).
- **Privacy is graduated.** A library can be entirely private, per-shelf visible, or public; products differ in the default.
definition.rules_zh:
- **记录，而非内容。** 产品从不呈现书籍文本。系统中的每个对象都是关于书籍的（身份、状态、观点）；阅读本身在别处进行。这是该类型最清晰的结构特征。
- **保留是常态。** 已完成的书籍不会被清除；它们会积累。图书馆的健康度由其完整性和增长衡量，而非空队列。
- **状态通常互斥。** 在追踪器形态产品中，一本书通常一次只占据一个阅读状态——向前移动会将其移出前一个书架——而自定义书架/收藏集独立于状态持有书籍。（在采样的开源追踪器中明确记录；具体机制视产品而定。）
- **每本书一个共享身份。** 因为记录针对共享目录解析，两个读者引用同一本书即引用同一条记录——这正是社区书评和比较成为可能的原因。用户通常可以更正目录数据；部分产品将更正路由至员工审核。
- **图书馆是可移植的。** 导入/导出是预期属性；个人图书馆是其数据，可在产品间移动（但需注意将旧记录匹配到新目录是近似的）。
- **隐私是分级化的。** 图书馆可以完全私密、按书架可见或公开；产品在默认设置上存在差异。

definition.name: Collaborative Document Editor
definition.overview:
A **Collaborative Document Editor** is a hosted writing application in which the document itself is a shared object: several people can open the same document, edit it at the same time, and always see one merged current version.

The defining structure is small:

```text
Shared Persistent Document
└── Shared access — the document's audience is extended beyond its
    original author through the product's sharing mechanism
    └── Concurrent multi-user editing merged into a single live current version
```

Everything else commonly associated with modern products — rich text formatting, comment threads, review modes, version history, live cursors, workspaces, guest links — is standard or optional capability, not the definition. A minimal self-hosted collaborative editor with plain text, pseudonymous authors, and nothing else is still recognizably this Type; a powerful word processor used by one person with files passed around by email is not.

The Type sits in deliberate contrast with the single-user Document Editor. The single-editor world runs on a save–copy–pass-around loop with manual reconciliation; the collaborative world replaces that loop with a shared document and a system that keeps everyone's view consistent. The boundary between the two is visible inside the market itself: where a product also serves older local clients, those clients may fall back to the save-and-merge mode — the older behavior reappearing as a compatibility path.
definition.overview_zh:
一个**协作文档编辑器**是一种托管式写作应用，其中文档本身是一个共享对象：多人可以同时打开同一文档，同时编辑，并始终看到合并后的当前版本。

其定义性结构很小：

```text
共享持久化文档
└── 共享访问——通过产品的共享机制，文档的受众扩展至原始作者之外
     └── 并发多用户编辑合并为单一实时当前版本
```

现代产品通常关联的其他一切——富文本格式、评论线程、审阅模式、版本历史、实时光标、工作区、访客链接——都是标准或可选功能，而非定义。一个仅包含纯文本、匿名作者且无其他功能的极简自托管协作编辑器，仍可明确识别为此类型；而一个人使用、通过电子邮件传递文件的强大文字处理器则不属于此类型。

该类型与单用户文档编辑器形成刻意对比。单编辑器世界运行于保存-复制-传递循环，需手动协调；协作世界则以共享文档和保持所有人视图一致的系统取代该循环。两者边界在市场内部可见：当产品同时服务旧版本地客户端时，这些客户端可能回退到保存并合并模式——旧行为作为兼容性路径重现。
definition.dc:
**The document.** A durable, addressable unit of composition — a text-bearing document that persists independent of any user's session or device. Someone can return next week and find the document as it was left, with its accumulated content. The document is the thing that is shared, edited, discussed, versioned, and delivered. (The document grammar is prose-shaped: paragraphs, headings, lists, images, tables. The same collaboration machinery applied to a grid produces the sibling Collaborative Spreadsheet type; applied to slides, the Collaborative Presentation Editor.)

**Shared access.** The document's audience is extended beyond its original author through the product's sharing mechanism — by inviting named people, by granting an organization or team, or by distributing a link. Whoever is inside that audience can open the document; whoever is outside normally cannot. Sharing is both a convenience surface and the access-control boundary of the Type.

**Concurrent editing, one current version.** Multiple people can edit at the same time, and the system integrates everyone's changes into a single current version that all participants see. There is no "whose copy wins" problem in normal flow: the merged document simply is the document. Editing is therefore continuous — changes are visible to co-editors as they happen, and the saved state advances as people type rather than only when someone remembers to save.

Remove shared access and the product collapses into a single-user Document Editor with a cloud copy. Remove concurrent-merged editing and it collapses into the save–copy–pass-around loop. Remove the persistent document and it becomes an ephemeral live surface rather than a writing tool.
definition.dc_zh: **文档。** 一个持久、可寻址的创作单元——一个承载文本的文档，独立于任何用户的会话或设备而持续存在。某人下周返回时，可以找到文档被留下的样子，包含其累积的内容。文档是被共享、编辑、讨论、版本控制和交付的东西。（文档语法是散文形状的：段落、标题、列表、图片、表格。相同的协作机制应用于网格，产生兄弟类型协同电子表格；应用于幻灯片，产生协同演示文稿编辑器。）**共享访问。** 文档的受众通过产品的共享机制扩展到原始作者之外——通过邀请指定的人、授予组织或团队、或分发链接。在该受众内的任何人都可以打开文档；通常之外的人则不能。共享既是便捷表面，也是类型的访问控制边界。**并发编辑，一个当前版本。** 多个人可以同时编辑，系统将每个人的更改集成到一个所有参与者都看到的单一当前版本中。在正常流程中，没有“哪个副本获胜”的问题：合并后的文档就是文档本身。因此编辑是连续的——更改在发生时对协作者可见，并且保存状态随着人们输入而推进，而不是仅当保存时。
definition.rules:
### There is one current version

The system, not the users, reconciles concurrent edits. In normal flow users never merge conflicting copies; the merged text simply exists. Behavior in pathological conflict cases is an implementation matter and is not uniform across products.

### Access level caps what a participant can do

A viewer can read but not change; a commenter can remark but not edit; an editor can change the content; sharing rights are typically a separate, higher capability. Where a document lives inside a hierarchy, access rules commonly inherit downward, and some products resolve overlapping grants by giving the broadest applicable access — details vary and matter in organization-scale deployments.

### Sharing is the gate

Editing happens only inside the granted audience. People outside it hit a request-access flow rather than a failure. Revoking access removes the person's entry; what they saw while inside is a governance question products answer differently.

### Attribution is visible

Edits and comments carry their author. In review machinery, proposed changes are attributed per reviewer and can be filtered by person. In the most attribution-centric products, even every keystroke carries its author's color through the document's entire history. The degree varies; the principle is common.

### Review mode separates proposal from text

When a review mode is engaged, recorded changes are proposals: they display independently of the clean text, they can be accepted or rejected one at a time or in bulk, and acceptance is what changes the document. Some products let the document owner lock review mode on, or share a document in a review context where tracking cannot be turned off — review is then an enforced workflow, not a preference.

### The degraded mode marks the boundary

A product that also serves older desktop clients may support a mode where co-editors see each other's changes only after saving. In that mode the application is behaving as a plain single-user document editor over a shared copy — and at least one major product documents exactly this fallback, which illustrates what the Type adds: the live merge.

### History accumulates by itself

Because editing is continuous and multi-user, history is gathered as a background property of editing rather than as explicit user saves (with explicit snapshots additionally available in some products). Restoring history is itself a change to the shared document, made within the same access rules.
definition.rules_zh:
### 存在单一当前版本

系统而非用户协调并发编辑。在正常流程中，用户从不合并冲突副本；合并文本直接存在。病态冲突案例中的行为是实现事项，各产品不统一。

### 访问级别限制参与者可执行操作

查看者可读但不可改；评论者可备注但不可编辑；编辑者可更改内容；共享权限通常为独立更高能力。当文档位于层级内时，访问规则通常向下继承，部分产品通过授予最宽适用访问解决重叠授权——细节各异，在组织规模部署中至关重要。

### 共享是入口

编辑仅在已授予受众内发生。外部人员触发请求访问流程而非失败。撤销访问移除该人员入口；其在内部所见内容属治理问题，各产品回答不同。

### 归属可见

编辑与评论携带其作者。在审阅机制中，提议更改按审阅者归属，可按人员筛选。在最具归属中心的产品中，甚至每次击键均携带作者颜色贯穿文档整个历史。程度各异；原则共通。

### 审阅模式分离提议与文本

当启用审阅模式时，记录更改为提议：独立于干净文本显示，可逐个或批量接受或拒绝，接受即更改文档。部分产品允许文档所有者锁定审阅模式开启，或在审阅上下文中共享文档，其中追踪不可关闭——此时审阅为强制工作流，非偏好。
